title: Reduction in neural-tube defects after folic acid fortification in Canada
authors: De Wals P, Tairou F, Van Allen MI, Uh SH, Lowry RB, Sibbald B, et al.
followUp: Births from 1993 to 2002, divided into prefortification, partial-fortification and full-fortification periods
population: Live births, stillbirths and terminations of pregnancy for fetal anomalies among women resident in seven Canadian provinces; 2446 neural tube defects among 1.9 million births
funder: Supported by a grant (MOP-57904) from the Canadian Institutes of Health Research.
authorConflicts: No potential conflict of interest relevant to this article was reported.
result: Population-based comparison before and after mandatory folic acid fortification of cereal products from 1998, at 0.15 mg per 100 g of flour or cornmeal. Prevalence of neural tube defects 1.58 per 1000 births before fortification and 0.86 per 1000 during full fortification, a 46% reduction (95% CI 40 to 51); calculated from these rates, 0.72 fewer per 1000 births. Reductions of 53% for spina bifida, 38% for anencephaly and 31% for encephalocele; the decrease was proportional to the baseline rate in each province.
